frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (tech transfer bottlenecks, specialized tooling shortages, facility hardening needs, quality assurance failures) prevent successful domestic operationalization within the target window?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states attempting domestic manufacturing or final assembly of advanced Western-designed tactical missile systems (cruise, air defense, or anti-ship) originally engineered elsewhere. Excludes simple small arms, unguided munitions, or domestic designs built from scratch.
window: Within a 3 to 5 year wartime timeline

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng III scaling and domestic tech maturation
Pakistan Babur cruise missile domestic production initiation
Ukraine Neptune domestic missile production establishment post-2014
India BrahMos joint venture manufacturing facility establishment
Iran Soumar (Kh-55 reverse engineering) production line setup

coverage_note: 5 named; small population due to extreme rarity of sovereign states attempting high-complexity cruise missile domestic lines.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral transfers where production assistance is covert and unverified.
skeleton: Total documented attempts at establishing complex foreign or reverse-engineered missile lines under strict deadlines; numerator is successful operationalization within window.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 documented attempts in relevant classes
validity_reason: Defense industrial base constraints and Western export control regimes evolve slowly over multi-year periods.
